title: Zone-local least-inflight replay
scenario: Replay ten seconds of traffic against a worker pool with health transitions. Requests stay in their zone and go to the lowest running/effective-weight worker (degraded halves the weight). Report assignments, per-worker load and rejections.

verified.why_correct: The `<=` matches rule 1 (transitions at or before the arrival apply), and the cursor only moves forward because events are sorted by time in load_health.

Plain tuple sorting puts (t, -1) before (t, 1), so a request that ends exactly when another starts is counted as finished first, as the spec asks. It looks like it needs an explicit sort key, but it doesn't.

bugs.title: Degraded check compares the enum to a string
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_1_east_assignments: e05 goes to east-2 instead of east-1, and e06 to east-1 instead of east-2. Every other zone is unaffected.
bugs.why: Worker states are WorkerState members, and a plain Enum never equals its value string. So the check is never true, east-2 keeps its full weight while degraded, and it wins ties it should lose.
hints: east-2 is the only worker that is degraded while traffic arrives. Does it ever look less attractive than east-1?
Look at how effective_weight decides whether a worker is degraded.
`worker.state == "degraded"` is always False for an Enum; compare with `is WorkerState.DEGRADED`.
probes: Why does `parse_state(...) == "degraded"` fail even though WorkerState.DEGRADED.value is "degraded"?
Why were e01 to e04 still right with the comparison broken?

bugs.title: Request ending at the arrival time still counted as running
bugs.old: w.inflight = [end for end in w.inflight if end > now_ms]
bugs.new: w.inflight = [end for end in w.inflight if end >= now_ms]
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_2_west_assignments: w02 goes to west-2 instead of west-1, and w03 to west-1 instead of west-2.
bugs.why: Rule 2 says a request ending at or before the new arrival has finished. Keeping `end >= now` leaves w01 (ends 12:00:02) on west-1 when w02 arrives at exactly 12:00:02, so w02 goes to west-2 and w03 flips too.
hints: Compare w01's end time with w02's arrival time.
Look at how finished requests are dropped before routing.
release_finished keeps `end >= now_ms`; the spec wants `end > now_ms`.
probes: Why does only the west zone notice this?
stats.peak_inflight has the same boundary rule. Where is it enforced there?

bugs.title: Utilisation rounded before scaling to a percentage
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_3_central_utilisation: cen-1 shows 114.99999999999999 instead of 115.0; the other central workers are exact.
bugs.why: Rounding the fraction and then multiplying by 100 brings binary float error back in, so 1.15 * 100 is 114.99999999999999. Scale first and round last.
hints: cen-1 shows 114.99999999999999. Where could the trailing 9s come from?
Look at the order of rounding and multiplying in utilisation_pct.
probes: Why do 52.0 and 33.0 come out exact but 115.0 doesn't?
Would round(x * 100, 1) after round(x, 3) be safe? Why or why not?

bugs.title: Peak counter carried across workers
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_4_central_peak_inflight: every central worker reports peak 3 (cen-1 is right; cen-2 should be 2, cen-3 1, cen-4 0).
bugs.why: `peak` is set once before the loop, so each worker reports the running maximum of every worker before it in id order. cen-1's 3 leaks into cen-2, cen-3 and cen-4.
hints: Every central worker after cen-1 has the same peak as cen-1. Is that plausible for cen-4, which served nothing?
Look at where peak and current are initialised in worker_stats.
Move `peak = 0` inside the per-worker loop, next to `current = 0`.
probes: Why was `current` fine even though it is also a running counter?
Which ordering of workers would have hidden this from the test?

bugs.title: max_inflight 0 replaced by the default
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_5_rejected: only s01 is rejected; n02 and n06 are missing because north-2 served them.
bugs.why: `or` treats an explicit 0 as missing, so the provisioning worker north-2 gets the default capacity of 2 and absorbs the north requests that should be rejected.
hints: n02 and n06 should have nowhere to go. Which worker took them?
Look at how the loader fills in max_inflight.
`item.get("max_inflight") or DEFAULT_MAX_INFLIGHT` turns 0 into 2; use item.get("max_inflight", DEFAULT_MAX_INFLIGHT).
probes: cen-2 has no max_inflight at all. Why did it behave the same with and without the change?
Why didn't any test on assignments notice north-2 taking traffic?

bugs.title: Out-of-rotation filter always true
bugs.old: if w.state is WorkerState.DOWN or w.state is WorkerState.DRAINING
bugs.new: if w.state is WorkerState.DOWN or WorkerState.DRAINING
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_6_out_of_rotation: all 13 workers are listed instead of cen-4, east-3, west-2, west-3.
bugs.why: The condition parses as `(w.state is DOWN) or WorkerState.DRAINING`, and an Enum member is truthy, so every worker passes the filter.
hints: Every worker is listed, including healthy ones. What does the filter evaluate to for a healthy worker?
Read the condition in out_of_rotation operator by operator.
Compare w.state on both sides of the `or` (or use `w.state in (DOWN, DRAINING)`).
probes: Why is WorkerState.DRAINING truthy on its own?
Why does this only show up in the summary?

context_qa.q: What happens inside replay() for each request?
context_qa.a: It calls `feed.apply_due(arrival)` to apply health transitions, `release_finished(workers, arrival)` to drop finished requests, then `pick_worker` on the workers of the request's zone. The chosen worker gets the request's end time appended to `inflight`; with no candidate the assignment is None. After the loop it calls `feed.flush()`.
A list of end times in ms, one per running request. `len(inflight)` is the number of running requests used by `has_room` and the score in `pick_worker`.
It takes `min` over eligible workers with the key `(len(inflight) / effective_weight(w), worker_id)`, so equal scores fall back to the worker id string.

context_qa.q: What type is Worker.state after loading and after a health event?
context_qa.a: `parse_state` returns a `WorkerState` member (a plain `Enum`, not a `str` subclass). Health events are parsed with the same function, and `apply_due` assigns `event.state` to the worker.

context_qa.q: How does worker_stats work out peak_inflight?
context_qa.a: For each worker it builds (arrival, end) intervals of its requests, turns them into (time, ±1) points with `sweep_points`, walks them in sorted order adding the deltas to `current`, and keeps the largest value seen in `peak`.

context_qa.q: What does load_requests return, and in what order?
context_qa.a: A list of `Request` objects sorted by `arrival_ms` with Python's stable sort, so same-time requests keep file order. A blank zone becomes `DEFAULT_ZONE` ("central").
In `build_report`, after `replay` has returned. `replay` ends with `feed.flush()`, which applies any remaining health transitions, so it reads each worker's final state.
